attrs.content: A shared world of inquiry: connecting ideas, evidence and the choices we make. Compare three review methods on the same evidence.

children: Claimipedia / A shared world of inquiry

Claimipedia is a framework for versioned claims, evidence and explicit review methods. It keeps the question, its scope, its sources and the method of judgment connected—so people can inspect a conclusion, understand a disagreement and revisit it.

attrs.aria-label: Three overlapping lenses connect the world, the ways we investigate it, and the choices we make.

children: One shared world. More than one way to understand it.
Give each claim a stable identity, a version and a stated scope. Keep evidence attached to the claim without treating its inclusion as proof that the claim is true.
Show the route to the answer.

Make review methods explicit: what evidence they admit, how they weigh it, and what is enough to decide. Different methods can reach different conclusions without being collapsed into a universal truth score.
Retain the evidence, method and reasons behind a result. New evidence or a corrected method should invite a new review, with the earlier reasoning still available to inspect.
A living example / Try it yourself
A method decides what counts, how much it counts, and when there is enough to reach a conclusion. Change the evidence below. Watch all three methods read the same snapshot.
The North River restoration reduced mean nitrate concentration by at least 15 percent during 2025.
In everyday terms: did the restoration lower the average amount of nitrate measured in the river’s water by at least 15%?
North River monitoring sites; 2025 compared with 2024.
All names, evidence and conclusions in this example are invented. This demonstrates review rules; it establishes no environmental finding.
01 / Choose the evidence in this snapshot
Uncheck an item to explore its effect. The original record remains visible.
A credentialed, independent, peer-reviewed study. Not retracted.
An independently collected dataset from a second laboratory. Source is not credentialed.
An independent community panel’s observations. Retraction status is not recorded.
A retracted, credentialed study from the same North laboratory. Not an independent source.

Here, “credentialed” means the source is marked as having recognised expertise. “Peer reviewed” means other researchers checked the work. “Independent” is a recorded source property in this fictional example; the page does not verify it.
Turn on JavaScript to change the evidence and inspect the comparison. The claim and evidence above remain readable.

Points are authored weights, not probabilities or percentages of truth. The marker on each bar is that method’s decision threshold. Independent sources are counted only among the evidence that the method admits.
Remove the retracted study. Equal weight changes because it counted that item. The other methods already excluded it. A transparent rule can still be a poor rule for a particular question.
The independent-source method can admit two supporting items and still withhold judgment: 0.9 points is below its 1.2-point threshold. More evidence and a lower threshold are different changes.
How the algebra makes this inspectable

One versioned claim and one selected evidence set feed three versioned methods. For each item, the process checks every condition, selects the highest-priority matching rule, then adds its weight to support or challenge. It counts distinct independent sources before testing the thresholds.
Missing information fails a condition. A retracted item stays in the record even when a method excludes it. Method results remain separate; they are never averaged into a universal score.

The page, styles, review rules, interaction and reasoning display are process queries and REL data, running on the same algebra as Temple and Sourcery. This bounded example is checked against all 48 original method-and-evidence combinations.
Move from curiosity to investigation, from judgment to action—and stay willing to return.

The working example above evaluates three methods on fictional evidence. The broader design includes governed contribution and review; this microsite does not offer a full production knowledge platform.
Shared evidence. Visible methods. Room to revise.
